answer: Each identity must solve a fresh memory-hard puzzle every epoch, about 20 GPU-minutes, before its votes count. A public beacon seeds the puzzle at epoch start, so work can't be precomputed, and each solution is stamped with the account's own pigment, a hash of its key, so one solve can't be reused. Influence climbs a trellis: one rung per solved epoch, capped at five. 1,000 fakes cost 1,000 x 20 GPU-minutes per epoch, growing linearly. Weakness: rented GPUs, though memory-hardness keeps them barely faster than laptops, so renting doesn't cut the cost much.
